sanskrit: kuṇḍaloṣṇīṣadhārīṇi jātarūpasrajāni ca patitāni sma dṛśyante śirāṃsi raṇamūrdhani
english: Heads adorned with earrings and turbans, garlanded with gold, could be seen fallen at the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: viśikhonmathitair gātrair bāhubhiś ca sakārmukaiḥ sahastābharaṇaiś cānyaiḥ pracchannā bhāti medinī
english: The earth shone covered with limbs torn apart by arrows, and with arms still clutching bows, adorned with bracelets and other ornaments.

sanskrit: śirasāṃ pātyamānānām antarā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ aśmavṛṣṭir ivākāśād abhavad bharatarṣabha
english: O bull of the Bhārata line, as heads were being felled by sharp arrows, it was as though a rain of stones fell from the sky.

sanskrit: darśayitvā tathātmānaṃ raudraṃ rudraparākramaḥ avaruddhaś caran pārtho daśavarṣāṇi trīṇi ca krodhāgnim utsṛjad ghoraṃ dhārtarāṣṭreṣu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Having thus revealed his terrible form, with the valor of Rudra himself, Pārtha the son of Pāṇḍu — who had been constrained and wandering for thirteen years — now unleashed the dreadful fire of his wrath upon the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tasya tad dahataḥ sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā caiva parākramam sarve śāntiparā yodhā dhārtarāṣṭrasya paśyataḥ
english: Seeing him burn the army and beholding his valor, all the warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son became intent on making peace, while their king looked on.

sanskrit: vitrāsayitvā tat sainyaṃ drāvayitvā mahārathān arjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ paryavartata bhārata
english: Having terrified that army and routed the great chariot-warriors, Arjuna, the foremost among the victorious, wheeled about, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prāvartayan nadīṃ ghorāṃ śoṇitaughataraṅgiṇīm asthiśaivalasaṃbādhāṃ yugānte kālanirmitām
english: He set in motion a dreadful river with waves of torrential blood, choked with bones serving as its moss, fashioned by Time at the end of an age.

sanskrit: śaracāpaplavāṃ ghorāṃ māṃsaśoṇitakardamām mahārathamahādvīpāṃ śaṅkhadundubhinisvanām cakāra mahatīṃ pārtho nadīm uttaraśoṇitām
english: Pārtha created a great and dreadful river flowing northward with blood — its rafts were arrows and bows, its mud was flesh and gore, its great islands were mighty chariot-warriors, and it resounded with the sound of conches and drums.

sanskrit: ādadānasya hi śarān saṃdhāya ca vimuñcataḥ vikarṣataś ca gāṇḍīvaṃ na kiṃ cid dṛśyate 'ntaram
english: As he picked up arrows, nocked them, and released them, and as he drew the Gāṇḍīva bow, no interval whatsoever could be perceived in his actions.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha duryodhanaḥ karṇo duḥśāsanaviviṃśatī droṇaś ca saha putreṇa kṛpaś cātiratho raṇe
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Duryodhana, Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, Viviṃśati, Droṇa together with his son, and Kṛpa — an outstanding chariot-warrior in battle —

sanskrit: punar īyuḥ susaṃrabdhā dhanaṃjayajighāṃsayā visphārayantaś cāpāni balavanti dṛḍhāni ca
english: — came forward again in great fury, with the desire to slay Dhanañjaya, twanging their powerful and sturdy bows.

sanskrit: tān prakīrṇapatākena rathenādityavarcasā pratyudyayau mahārāja samastān vānaradhvajaḥ
english: O great king, the one with the monkey banner advanced to meet them all together in his chariot, whose scattered pennants blazed like the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛpaś ca karṇaś ca droṇaś ca rathināṃ varaḥ taṃ mahāstrair mahāvīryaṃ parivārya dhanaṃjayam
english: Then Kṛpa, Karṇa, and Droṇa — the foremost among chariot-warriors — surrounded Dhanañjaya, that man of immense valor, with great celestial weapons.

sanskrit: śaraughān samyag asyanto jīmūtā iva vārṣikāḥ vavarṣuḥ śaravarṣāṇi prapatantaṃ kirīṭinam
english: Releasing volleys of arrows accurately, like monsoon clouds in the rainy season, they rained down showers of arrows upon the diademed warrior as he advanced.

sanskrit: iṣubhir bahubhis tūrṇaṃ samare lomavāhibhiḥ adūrāt paryavasthāya pūrayām āsur ādṛtāḥ
english: Taking their stand nearby in battle, they diligently filled him quickly with many arrows that caused the hair to stand on end.

sanskrit: tathāvakīrṇasya hi tair divyair astraiḥ samantataḥ na tasya dvyaṅgulam api vivṛtaṃ samadṛśyata
english: As he was covered on all sides by those divine weapons, not even two finger-breadths of his body remained uncovered.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya bībhatsur divyam aindraṃ mahārathaḥ astram ādityasaṃkāśaṃ gāṇḍīve samayojayat
english: Then Bībhatsu, that great chariot-warrior, smiled and invoked upon the Gāṇḍīva the divine weapon of Indra, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: sa raśmibhir ivādityaḥ pratapan samare balī kirīṭamālī kaunteyaḥ sarvān prācchādayat kurūn
english: Like the sun with its rays, the mighty diademed son of Kuntī, blazing in battle, covered over all the Kurus.

sanskrit: yathā balāhake vidyut pāvako vā śiloccaye tathā gāṇḍīvam abhavad indrāyudham ivātatam
english: Just as lightning flashes in a storm-cloud, or fire blazes on a rocky mountain, so the Gāṇḍīva appeared like Indra's own weapon stretched wide.

sanskrit: yathā varṣati parjanye vidyud vibhrājate divi tathā daśa diśaḥ sarvāḥ patad gāṇḍīvam āvṛṇot
english: Just as lightning blazes in the sky when the rain-cloud pours down, so the flying Gāṇḍīva covered all ten directions.

sanskrit: trastāś ca rathinaḥ sarve babhūvus tatra sarvaśaḥ sarve śāntiparā bhūtvā svacittāni na lebhire saṃgrāmavimukhāḥ sarve yodhās te hatacetasaḥ
english: All the chariot-warriors everywhere became terrified; becoming intent on peace, they could not collect their own thoughts. All those warriors turned their faces away from battle, their spirits broken.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvāṇi sainyāni bhagnāni bharatarṣabha prādravanta diśaḥ sarvā nirāśāni svajīvite
english: Thus, O bull of the Bhārata line, all the armies were broken and fled in every direction, without hope for their own lives.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo durādharṣaḥ pratāpavān vadhyamāneṣu yodheṣu dhanaṃjayam upādravat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu — irresistible and of great prowess — charged at Dhanañjaya while the warriors were being slaughtered.

sanskrit: pragṛhya kārmukaśreṣṭhaṃ jātarūpapariṣkṛtam śarān ādāya tīkṣṇāgrān marmabhedapramāthinaḥ
english: Taking up his finest bow adorned with gold, and taking sharp-tipped arrows capable of piercing the vital points and causing destruction —

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani śuśubhe sa naravyāghro giriḥ sūryodaye yathā
english: — that tiger among men, with a white umbrella held above his head, shone like a mountain at sunrise.

sanskrit: pradhmāya śaṅkhaṃ gāṅgeyo dhārtarāṣṭrān praharṣayan pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya bībhatsuṃ samavārayat
english: Blowing his conch and filling the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with joy, the son of the Gaṅgā circled to the right and checked Bībhatsu.

sanskrit: tam udvīkṣya tathāyāntaṃ kaunteyaḥ paravīrahā pratyagṛhṇāt prahṛṣṭātmā dhārādharam ivācalaḥ
english: Beholding him coming thus, the son of Kuntī, slayer of enemy heroes, received him with joyful spirit, like a mountain receiving a rain-bearing cloud.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmaḥ śarān aṣṭau dhvaje pārthasya vīryavān samaparyan mahāvegāñ śvasamānān ivoragān
english: Then valiant Bhīṣma shot eight arrows of great speed into Pārtha's banner — arrows hissing like serpents.

sanskrit: te dhvajaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya samāsādya patatriṇaḥ jvalantaḥ kapim ājaghnur dhvajāgranilayāṃś ca tān
english: Those feathered and blazing arrows, reaching the banner of the son of Pāṇḍu, struck the monkey and those other beings dwelling at the top of the standard.

sanskrit: tato bhallena mahatā pṛthudhāreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ chatraṃ ciccheda bhīṣmasya tūrṇaṃ tad apatad bhuvi
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu swiftly cut Bhīṣma's umbrella with a great broad-bladed arrow, and it fell to the ground.

sanskrit: dhvajaṃ caivāsya kaunteyaḥ śarair abhyahanad dṛḍham śīghrakṛd rathavāhāṃś ca tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī
english: The son of Kuntī, swift in action, also struck his banner hard with arrows, and likewise both his horses, his chariot-drivers, and both rear-guard warriors.

sanskrit: tayos tad abhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam bhīṣmasya saha pārthena balivāsavayor iva
english: The tumultuous and hair-raising battle between Bhīṣma and Pārtha was like that of Bali and Vāsava (Indra).

sanskrit: bhallair bhallāḥ samāgamya bhīṣmapāṇḍavayor yudhi antarikṣe vyarājanta khadyotāḥ prāvṛṣīva hi
english: In the battle between Bhīṣma and the Pāṇḍava, broad-headed arrows meeting broad-headed arrows glittered in the sky like fireflies in the rainy season.

sanskrit: agnicakram ivāviddhaṃ savyadakṣiṇam asyataḥ gāṇḍīvam abhavad rājan pārthasya sṛjataḥ śarān
english: O king, the Gāṇḍīva of Pārtha as he released arrows, shooting to the left and right, appeared like a spinning wheel of fire.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ saṃchādayām āsa bhīṣmaṃ śaraśataiḥ śitaiḥ parvataṃ vāridhārābhiś chādayann iva toyadaḥ
english: He covered Bhīṣma with hundreds of sharp arrows, like a rain-cloud covering a mountain with streams of water.

sanskrit: tāṃ sa velām ivoddhūtāṃ śaravṛṣṭiṃ samutthitām vyadhamat sāyakair bhīṣmo arjunaṃ saṃnivārayat
english: Bhīṣma dispersed that rising shower of arrows, like a wave tossed up by the sea, with his own shafts and checked Arjuna.

sanskrit: tatas tāni nikṛttāni śarajālāni bhāgaśaḥ samare 'bhivyaśīryanta phalgunasya rathaṃ prati
english: Then those nets of arrows, cut apart piece by piece in battle, fell scattered toward Phalguna's chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakapuṅkhānāṃ śaravṛṣṭiṃ samutthitām pāṇḍavasya rathāt tūrṇaṃ śalabhānām ivāyatim vyadhamat tāṃ punas tasya bhīṣmaḥ śaraśataiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Then the rising shower of gold-fletched arrows from the Pāṇḍava's chariot — coming swiftly like a swarm of locusts — Bhīṣma in turn dispersed with hundreds of sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tatas te kuravaḥ sarve sādhu sādhv iti cābruvan duṣkaraṃ kṛtavān bhīṣmo yad arjunam ayodhayat
english: Then all the Kurus cried out "Bravo! Bravo!" saying that Bhīṣma had done a difficult thing in fighting Arjuna.

sanskrit: balavāṃs taruṇo dakṣaḥ kṣiprakārī ca pāṇḍavaḥ ko 'nyaḥ samarthaḥ pārthasya vegaṃ dhārayituṃ raṇe
english: The Pāṇḍava is powerful, young, skilled, and swift in action — who else is capable of withstanding Pārtha's speed in battle?

sanskrit: ṛte śāṃtanavād bhīṣmāt kṛṣṇād vā devakīsutāt ācāryapravarād vāpi bhāradvājān mahābalāt
english: — except Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, or Kṛṣṇa the son of Devakī, or the foremost of teachers, Bhāradvāja's son of great strength.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya krīḍataḥ puruṣarṣabhau cakṣūṃṣi sarvabhūtānāṃ mohayantau mahābalau
english: Those two bulls among men, of great power, countering weapons with weapons as if at play, bewildered the eyes of all creatures.

sanskrit: prājāpatyaṃ tathaivaindram āgneyaṃ ca sudāruṇam kauberaṃ vāruṇaṃ caiva yāmyaṃ vāyavyam eva ca prayuñjānau mahātmānau samare tau viceratuḥ
english: Those two great-souled ones moved about in battle employing the weapons of Prajāpati, Indra, the terrible weapon of Agni, those of Kubera, Varuṇa, Yama, and the wind-god.

sanskrit: vismitāny atha bhūtāni tau dṛṣṭvā saṃyuge tadā sādhu pārtha mahābāho sādhu bhīṣmeti cābruvan
english: Then all beings were astonished, seeing the two in combat, and cried out "Well done, Pārtha, mighty-armed! Well done, Bhīṣma!"

sanskrit: nedaṃ yuktaṃ manuṣyeṣu yo 'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate mahān mahāstrāṇāṃ saṃprayogaḥ samare bhīṣmapārthayoḥ
english: "This great deployment of celestial weapons that is seen in the battle between Bhīṣma and Pārtha is not fitting for mortals."

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvāstraviduṣor astrayuddham avartata atha jiṣṇur upāvṛtya pṛthudhāreṇa kārmukam cakarta bhīṣmasya tadā jātarūpapariṣkṛtam
english: Thus the weapon-battle of those two who knew all weapons continued. Then Jiṣṇu (Arjuna), wheeling about, cut Bhīṣma's bow adorned with gold, with a broad-bladed arrow.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa bhīṣmo 'nyat kārmukaṃ raṇe samādāya mahābāhuḥ sajyaṃ cakre mahābalaḥ śarāṃś ca subahūn kruddho mumocāśu dhanaṃjaye
english: In the mere twinkling of an eye, mighty-armed Bhīṣma of great strength took up another bow in battle, strung it, and in anger quickly released very many arrows at Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: arjuno 'pi śarāṃś citrān bhīṣmāya niśitān bahūn cikṣepa sumahātejās tathā bhīṣmaś ca pāṇḍave
english: Arjuna too, of very great energy, hurled many varied and sharp arrows at Bhīṣma, and Bhīṣma likewise hurled arrows at the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tayor divyāstraviduṣor asyator aniśaṃ śarān na viśeṣas tadā rājaṃl lakṣyate sma mahātmanoḥ
english: O king, as those two great-souled masters of celestial weapons released arrows ceaselessly, no difference between them could be perceived.

sanskrit: athāvṛṇod daśa diśaḥ śarair atirathas tadā kirīṭamālī kaunteyaḥ śūraḥ śāṃtanavas tathā
english: Then the diademed son of Kuntī, that supreme chariot-warrior, covered the ten directions with arrows, and likewise the brave son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: atīva pāṇḍavo bhīṣmaṃ bhīṣmaś cātīva pāṇḍavam babhūva tasmin saṃgrāme rājaṃl loke tad adbhutam
english: O king, the Pāṇḍava surpassed Bhīṣma exceedingly, and Bhīṣma surpassed the Pāṇḍava exceedingly — in that battle it was a wonder to the world.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavena hatāḥ śūrā bhīṣmasya ratharakṣiṇaḥ śerate sma tadā rājan kaunteyasyābhito ratham
english: O king, the heroic chariot-guards of Bhīṣma, slain by the Pāṇḍava, lay all around the chariot of the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvanirmuktā niramitraṃ cikīrṣavaḥ āgacchan puṅkhasaṃśliṣṭāḥ śvetavāhanapatriṇaḥ
english: Then the feathered arrows of the white-horsed warrior, loosed from the Gāṇḍīva and desiring to make an end of enemies, came forward, tightly bound at the nock.

sanskrit: niṣpatanto rathāt tasya dhautā hairaṇyavāsasaḥ ākāśe samadṛśyanta haṃsānām iva paṅktayaḥ
english: Leaping forth from his chariot, gleaming and clothed in gold, they appeared in the sky like lines of swans.

sanskrit: tasya tad divyam astraṃ hi pragāḍhaṃ citram asyataḥ prekṣante smāntarikṣasthāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ
english: As he released that wondrous and deeply potent divine weapon, all the gods together with Vāsava (Indra) who stood in the sky looked on.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā paramaprīto gandharvaś citram adbhutam śaśaṃsa devarājāya citrasenaḥ pratāpavān
english: Seeing that marvelous and wondrous feat, the illustrious gandharva Citrasena, supremely pleased, reported it to the king of the gods.

sanskrit: paśyemān arinirdārān saṃsaktān iva gacchataḥ citrarūpam idaṃ jiṣṇor divyam astram udīryataḥ
english: "See these enemy-destroyers going as if linked together — this is the wondrous form of Jiṣṇu's divine weapon as it blazes forth."

sanskrit: nedaṃ manuṣyāḥ śraddadhyur na hīdaṃ teṣu vidyate paurāṇānāṃ mahāstrāṇāṃ vicitro 'yaṃ samāgamaḥ
english: "Mortals would not believe this — indeed it does not exist among them. This wondrous conjunction of ancient great weapons is beyond them."

sanskrit: madhyaṃdinagataṃ sūryaṃ pratapantam ivāmbare na śaknuvanti sainyāni pāṇḍavaṃ prativīkṣitum
english: Like the sun blazing in the sky at midday, the armies could not look directly at the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: ubhau viśrutakarmāṇāv ubhau yuddhaviśāradau ubhau sadṛśakarmāṇāv ubhau yudhi durāsadau
english: Both were celebrated for their deeds, both were skilled in battle, both performed equal feats, both were unapproachable in combat.

sanskrit: ity ukto devarājas tu pārthabhīṣmasamāgamam pūjayām āsa divyena puṣpavarṣeṇa bhārata
english: Thus addressed, O Bhārata, the king of the gods honored the encounter of Pārtha and Bhīṣma with a divine shower of flowers.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo vāme pārśve samarpayat asyataḥ pratisaṃdhāya vivṛtaṃ savyasācinaḥ
english: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, having taken aim and found an opening, planted a shaft in the left side of Savyasācin (Arjuna) as he was shooting.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya bībhatsuḥ pṛthudhāreṇa kārmukam nyakṛntad gārdhrapatreṇa bhīṣmasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Then Bībhatsu, smiling, cut the bow of Bhīṣma of immeasurable energy with a broad-bladed, vulture-feathered arrow.

sanskrit: athainaṃ daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare yatamānaṃ parākrāntaṃ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Then Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī, pierced him in the chest with ten arrows as he strove and pressed forward.

sanskrit: sa pīḍito mahābāhur gṛhītvā rathakūbaram gāṅgeyo yudhi durdharṣas tasthau dīrgham ivāturaḥ
english: Tormented, the mighty-armed son of the Gaṅgā — irresistible in battle — stood gripping the chariot-pole for a long time as if in pain.

sanskrit: taṃ visaṃjñam apovāha saṃyantā rathavājinām upadeśam anusmṛtya rakṣamāṇo mahāratham
english: The charioteer, recalling his instructions and protecting the great warrior, drove him away while he was insensible.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhīṣme tu saṃgrāmaśiro vihāya; palāyamāne dhṛtarāṣṭraputraḥ ucchritya ketuṃ vinadan mahātmā; svayaṃ vigṛhyārjunam āsasāda
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Bhīṣma had abandoned the head of battle and fled, the great-souled son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra raised his standard and, roaring, came himself to grapple with Arjuna.

sanskrit: sa bhīmadhanvānam udagravīryaṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ śatrugaṇe carantam ākarṇapūrṇāyatacoditena; bhallena vivyādha lalāṭamadhye
english: He pierced Dhanañjaya — wielder of the mighty bow, of lofty valor, ranging among the throng of enemies — right in the middle of the forehead with a broad-bladed arrow drawn fully to the ear.

sanskrit: sa tena bāṇena samarpitena; jāmbūnadābhena susaṃśitena rarāja rājan mahanīyakarmā; yathaikaparvā ruciraikaśṛṅgaḥ
english: Struck by that well-aimed arrow of refined gold, O king, the doer of noble deeds shone like a single-knotted, beautiful single-peaked mountain.

sanskrit: athāsya bāṇena vidāritasya; prādurbabhūvāsṛg ajasram uṣṇam sā tasya jāmbūnadapuṣpacitrā; māleva citrābhivirājate sma
english: Then from him, pierced by the arrow, warm blood flowed freely — that garland of gold-colored flowers upon him shone resplendent with its varied hues.

sanskrit: sa tena bāṇābhihatas tarasvī; duryodhanenoddhatamanyuvegaḥ śarān upādāya viṣāgnikalpān; vivyādha rājānam adīnasattvaḥ
english: Struck by that arrow, the swift and undaunted warrior, his anger aroused by Duryodhana, took up arrows like poison and fire and pierced the king.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś cāpi tam ugratejāḥ; pārthaś ca duryodhanam ekavīraḥ anyonyam ājau puruṣapravīrau; samaṃ samājaghnatur ājamīḍhau
english: And Duryodhana of fierce energy struck him, and Pārtha the sole hero struck Duryodhana — those two foremost heroes of the Ajamīḍha clan struck each other equally in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhinnena mahāgajena; mahīdharābhena punar vikarṇaḥ rathaiś caturbhir gajapādarakṣaiḥ; kuntīsutaṃ jiṣṇum athābhyadhāvat
english: Then Vikarṇa, with a great elephant in rut resembling a moving mountain, along with four chariots protecting the elephant's flanks, charged at Jiṣṇu, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ tvaritaṃ gajendraṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ kumbhavibhāgamadhye ākarṇapūrṇena dṛḍhāyasena; bāṇena vivyādha mahājavena
english: Dhanañjaya pierced that lord of elephants charging swiftly right between the frontal lobes with a swift, firm iron arrow drawn fully to the ear.

sanskrit: pārthena sṛṣṭaḥ sa tu gārdhrapatra; ā puṅkhadeśāt praviveśa nāgam vidārya śailapravaraprakāśaṃ; yathāśaniḥ parvatam indrasṛṣṭaḥ
english: That vulture-feathered arrow released by Pārtha entered the elephant all the way to the nock, tearing through that creature radiant as a great mountain — like a thunderbolt sent by Indra into a peak.

sanskrit: śaraprataptaḥ sa tu nāgarājaḥ; pravepitāṅgo vyathitāntarātmā saṃsīdamāno nipapāta mahyāṃ; vajrāhataṃ śṛṅgam ivācalasya
english: That king of elephants, scorched by the arrow, his limbs trembling and his inner spirit tormented, sinking down, fell to the earth like the peak of a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: nipātite dantivare pṛthivyāṃ; trāsād vikarṇaḥ sahasāvatīrya tūrṇaṃ padāny aṣṭaśatāni gatvā; viviṃśateḥ syandanam āruroha
english: When the finest of tusked elephants fell to the earth, Vikarṇa in fear instantly descended and, quickly going eight hundred paces, mounted the chariot of Viviṃśati.

sanskrit: nihatya nāgaṃ tu śareṇa tena; vajropamenādrivarāmbudābham tathāvidhenaiva śareṇa pārtho; duryodhanaṃ vakṣasi nirbibheda
english: Having slain the elephant with that arrow — that arrow like a thunderbolt, like the best of mountains, like a rain-cloud — with that same kind of arrow Pārtha then pierced Duryodhana in the chest.

sanskrit: tato gaje rājani caiva bhinne; bhagne vikarṇe ca sapādarakṣe gāṇḍīvamuktair viśikhaiḥ praṇunnās; te yodhamukhyāḥ sahasāpajagmuḥ
english: Then, with both the elephant and the king struck down, and Vikarṇa along with his foot-guards routed, those foremost warriors, driven away by the shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, suddenly fled.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva bāṇena hataṃ tu nāgaṃ; yodhāṃś ca sarvān dravato niśamya rathaṃ samāvṛtya kurupravīro; raṇāt pradudrāva yato na pārthaḥ
english: Seeing the elephant felled by the arrow and learning that all his warriors were fleeing, that foremost hero of the Kurus turned his chariot and fled from the battle to where Pārtha was not.
